name: Morkulangara Devi Temple
significance: A Bhagavathi shrine at Vazhappally in Changanassery completed under the Thekkumkur kings and now administered by the Travancore Devaswom Board. Its image stands over six feet tall, unusually large for a Kerala temple, and the three-day Meena Bharani festival is its principal celebration.
story: The goddess is said to have settled at this spot after destroying the demon Darika.

name: Neelkantheshwar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Pali in Lalitpur district built around an unusual three-headed image of the god. It draws a large fair on Maha Shivaratri, when devotees process to the shrine.
story: Local belief holds that the three-headed image emerged from the mountain of its own accord and the temple was raised around it.

name: Mallikarjunar Temple, Dharmapuri
deity: Shiva (Mallikarjunar), with the goddess Kamatchi Ammai
significance: A Shiva temple within the old Athiyaman fort at Dharmapuri, counted among the Vaippu Sthalams praised in the hymns of the Nayanar Sundarar. It also holds the samadhi shrine of Siddhalingesvarar, which receives the first worship of the day, along with shrines to Yoga Narasimha, Virabhadra, Bhairava and Surya.

name: Bhayankavu Bhagavathi Temple
significance: A goddess temple near Tirur whose square sanctum holds a granite image of the Mother Goddess along with subsidiary deities. It is best known for the Thalappoli observance in the Malayalam month of Kumbam, with Kalamezhuthu floor drawings and Poothan and Thira folk performances.

name: Sri Vinayaka Temple, Guddattu
significance: A Ganesha temple near Kundapura established in the 13th century and described as the only Jaladhivasa Ganapathi shrine in India. It is held in the ancestry of the Guddattu Adiga family and observes daily rites including Tailabhyanjana, Panchamrutha and Rudrabhisheka.
story: The three-foot image of Ganesha is believed to have emerged from the rock itself.

name: Dalavanur Cave Temple
significance: A rock-cut cave temple between Gingee and Mandagapattu attributed to the 7th-century Pallava king Mahendravarman I and thought to have been dedicated to Shiva. It is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India and is noted for its unusual inscriptions and for Jain rock beds cut above the cave.

name: Kudroli Bhagavathi Temple
deity: Bhagavathi, worshipped in fourteen forms under three names
significance: A Mangaluru goddess temple with a reported eight centuries of history, ranked as the Koota Kala among eighteen Bhagavathi temples across Karnataka and Kerala. Its precinct holds a Veera Sthambha and a marble statue of Narayana Guru, and the Bharani Utsav is held once every seven years.

name: Sri Madduramma Temple
significance: A village goddess temple at Huskur in Anekal taluk, described as one of the oldest in the Bengaluru area and dating to the Chola period. A grand annual festival is held there in March or April.

name: Cheranalloor Mahadeva Temple
significance: One of the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala and an important shrine of the former Cochin Kingdom, with a circular sanctum and a square namaskara mandapam. Before the agrarian reforms it drew an annual income of roughly 24 tons of paddy from extensive landholdings.
story: The sage Parashurama is said to have installed the Shiva image here in the Treta Yuga.

name: Marikamba Temple, Sagara
significance: Built in 1596 under Venkatappa Nayaka of the Keladi and Ikkeri kingdom, whose family held Marikamba as their tutelary deity. The shrine preserves the goddess's footprints, first consecrated on the town's outskirts and later moved to its centre, and hosts the triennial Marikamba Jathra with a sixteen-foot chariot.
story: Adi Shankaracharya is said to have been told by the goddess in a dream to establish her temple on this spot.

name: Kanimangalam Sastha Temple
significance: One of the temples that take part in the Thrissur Pooram, and the first of the poorams to enter the Vadakkunnathan temple. Its deity is regarded as the protector of the goddesses who join the festival, verifying arrangements for the other participating processions.

name: Kanjiramattam Sree Mahadeva Temple
significance: An old Shiva temple on the bank of the Thodupuzha river, counted among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala. The deity is shown seated in meditation beneath a kalpavriksha with Parvati, and the compound holds subsidiary shrines to Durga, Ganapati and Mookambika.
story: The lingam is traditionally said to have been installed by the sage Parasurama.

name: Pachaimalai Subramanya Swamy Temple
significance: A hill temple to Murugan near Gobichettipalayam, built in 1956 after a devotee reported a divine spark on the hillock in 1954 and enlarged in 1980. It has a five-tier gopuram and a forty-foot statue of the god, and the hill is named in the 17th-century Thirukutrala Kuravanji.
story: The sage Durvasa is said to have installed a chakra on the hillock, after which Murugan appeared there in the form of a serpent to grant darshan.

name: Kadachira Sri Thrikkapalam Siva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple on the Anjarakandy river that is unusual in housing two images of equal standing in separate sanctums. It is one of three Thrikkapaleeswaram shrines listed among Kerala's 108 Shiva temples, the others being at Niranam and Nadapuram, and its main festival is Maha Shivaratri.
story: Tradition holds that the sage Parasurama installed the image here.

name: Muttichur Kallattupuzha Sri Maha Siva Temple
significance: A west-facing Shiva temple on the bank of the Karuvannur river at Anthikad, counted among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala. It is referred to in the Malayalam poem Koka Sandesam.
story: Local lore credits the sage Parashurama with installing the temple's main image.

name: Ranganathaswamy Temple, Nirthadi
significance: A Vishnu temple rebuilt in 1698 by the Chitradurga chief Baramappa Nayaka after the earlier structure was destroyed by Aurangzeb's armies in 1696, as recorded by a Kannada inscription at the site and documented by Benjamin Lewis Rice. Now an ASI-protected monument, it retains an entrance mukhamantapa, yali pillars and a moulded frieze.

name: Chowara Chidambaraswamy Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Chowara whose east-facing northern sanctum enshrines the god in the dancing form of Nataraja, and which is reckoned among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala. Its main festival is Maha Shivaratri in the Malayalam month of Kumbha.
story: The temple is believed to have been founded by the sage Parasurama.

name: Kudappanakunnu Kunnathu Sri Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple on the northern edge of Thiruvananthapuram, reckoned among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala, with east-facing sanctums and subsidiary worship of Ganapathy and the serpent Vasuki. Its annual festival falls in the Malayalam month of Dhanu.
story: The shrine is believed to have been established by the sage Parasurama.

name: Yoga Nandeeshwara Temple
significance: A Shiva temple on Nandi Hills, also known as Nandidurg, in Chikkaballapur district. The article dates the shrine to the Chola period.

name: Nilakantheswar Temple
significance: A 7th-century Shiva shrine raised on seven rocks of the Jagamanda hills at Padmapur, where a rock inscription connects the site with the Buddhist logician Dharmakirti. Three further Shiva temples on the same hillock have made Padmapur a local pilgrimage and tourist centre.

name: Shivleni Caves
significance: Rock-cut Shiva caves at Ambajogai carrying an inscription of Saka 1066 associated with the Paramara king Udayaditya of Malwa, with a four-pillared pavilion opening on a hall carried by thirty-two pillars and sculptures of Shiva, the Saptamatrikas and Ganesha. They were described in Fergusson and Burgess's 1880 The Cave Temples of India and are a state-protected monument.
story: Local belief holds that the caves mark a wedding of the goddess Jogaidevi that could not be completed, at which the elephants and structures inside were turned to stone.

name: Shri Kala Bhairava Nath Swami Temple
significance: A temple to Bhairava in the old village of Adegaon in Seoni district, described as one of the better-known Bhairava shrines of the region.

name: Someshwara Temple, Marathahalli
significance: A Shiva temple at Marathahalli in eastern Bengaluru, recorded as having been completed in 1508. The Wikipedia entry is a short stub and carries maintenance notices about sourcing.

name: Shri Tilbhandeshwar Mahadev Mandir
significance: One of the older and better-known Shiva temples of Varanasi, believed to have been built in the 18th century in the Bhelupur quarter. Its lingam stands about three and a half feet high with a base roughly three feet across.
story: The lingam is said to have emerged of its own accord 2,500 years ago and to grow each year by the width of a sesame seed, from which the temple takes its name.

name: Sundaresvarar Temple, Kundayur
significance: One of the Vaippu Sthalams praised in the hymns of the Nayanar Sundarar, near Thirukkuvalai in Nagapattinam district. The temple has no gopuram but opens to both east and west, keeps two atti trees, and holds an annual Nel Atti Vizha during Masi Maham.
story: Sundarar is said to have asked the god at Tirukkuvalai to send on the paddy he had been given, and the deity had it delivered by his attendants.

name: Gopnath Mahadev Temple
significance: A shore temple to Shiva on the Gulf of Khambhat coast at Gopnath, described as nearly seven hundred years old and flying two flags for its Mahadev and Vishnu shrines. A fort of the ruler of Gohilwad also stands at the site.
story: The devotional poet Narsinh Mehta is said to have had his decisive spiritual experience at this Shiva temple some five centuries ago.

name: Mariyamma Temple
significance: A goddess temple at Urwa in Mangaluru raised roughly eight centuries ago by the Mogaveera fishing community, whose members offer gold ornaments shaped as mackerel, sardine, prawn and pomfret in thanksgiving. Fishermen have long prayed here during crises at sea, and the Mari Puja festival falls in early March.
story: A member of the Mogaveera community is said to have been possessed by the goddess and told by her to build a temple for her at Urwa.

name: Kote Anjaneya Temple
significance: A Hanuman temple at Tumakuru whose image was consecrated more than five centuries ago by Vyasaraja, rajaguru of the Vijayanagara empire and teacher of Kanakadasa and Purandaradasa, as one of 732 Hanuman images he installed across India. A 75-foot statue of the god was unveiled at its entrance in May 2005.

name: Swamithope Pathi
significance: The foremost of the five pathis of the Ayyavazhi tradition, in Kanyakumari district. Its inner Palliyarai keeps objects held to have been used by Ayya Vaikundar, including a rattan cane and wooden sandals, and the Ayya Vaikunda Avataram festival draws followers from across the country.
story: Followers hold that Vaikundar performed austerities at this spot for six years and was afterwards interred within the temple.

name: Agastheesvarar Temple, Kuzhaiyur
significance: A Shiva temple at Kuzhaiyur counted among the Vaippu Sthalams sung by the Nayanar Appar. It has no gopuram, only a walled entrance and a single prakaram, and holds further shrines to Subramanya, Kasi Visvanatha and Varadharaja Perumal; its last kumbhabhishekham was in July 2009.
story: When Shiva's wedding on Kailash tilted the earth's balance, he sent the sage Agastya south to restore it, and the sage is said to have worshipped here on that journey, giving the place its name.

name: Talikotta Mahadeva Temple
significance: One of the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala and one of the four thali temples named in the 108-temple hymn, where the god is worshipped in his fierce aspect. It was a principal shrine of the Thekkumkur kingdom, which Marthanda Varma annexed to Travancore after the Changanassery war of 1750.
story: Folklore credits the sage Parashurama with installing the Shiva image here.

name: Rajah Annamalaipuram Ayyappan Koil
significance: An Ayyappa temple on Santhome High Road in Chennai, founded in 1981 and consecrated in 1982 by the industrialist M. A. M. Ramaswamy Chettiar of the Chettinad group on land given by Rajah Sir Muthiah Chettiar, and built as a close copy of the Sabarimala shrine after his 1973 pilgrimage there. Its panchaloha image of Ayyappa, made by the sculptor Bhattanachariar, was installed on 25 January 1982.

name: Kulathupuzha Sastha Temple
significance: One of the five major Sastha temples of Kerala, where the deity is worshipped as a child and known as the Kulathupuzha Balakan; it is administered by the Travancore Devaswom Board. Devotees seeking relief from skin ailments make the Meenoottu offering of feeding the fish in its pond, which shelters the endangered Tor khudree and Hypselobarbus thomassi.
story: Sastha is said to have allowed a mermaid-like being drawn to him to live on in the temple pond in the form of a fish.

name: Karivellur Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple near Payyanur in Kannur district, counted among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala. It was formerly held by the Chirakkal Kovilakam.

name: Cheruvathur Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple about a kilometre from Kunnamkulam, reckoned among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala. Its east-facing sanctum is circular and roofed in copper.
story: Tradition holds that the sage Parasurama installed the image, as at the other temples of the 108 Shiva group.

name: Masilamaninathar Temple, Tharangambadi
significance: Built in 1306 by the Pandya king Maravarman Kulasekara Pandiyan I, this is one of the few surviving shore temples in India, standing 300 m north of the Danish Fort Dansborg. Its design mixes Tamil and Chinese elements, said to have been intended to draw Chinese merchants, and it is one of the Vaippu Sthalams sung by the Nayanars Appar and Sundarar.

name: Maa Pratyangira Kalika Alayam
significance: A temple at Moranapalli near Hosur devoted chiefly to Pratyangira, alongside Sharabha, Narasimha and Mariamman, and said to carry the largest image of the goddess, set on its gopuram. Worshippers offer garlands and light ghee lamps below the deity, and the temple draws heavy crowds through the week.

name: Sasthamangalam Mahadevar Temple
deity: Shiva as Uma Maheshwara, with Parvati
significance: A Shiva temple in the Sasthamangalam ward of Thiruvananthapuram, dated by surviving records to more than seven centuries ago. The kings of Travancore worshipped here regularly, and it is now run by the Travancore Devaswom Board.
story: A woman sharpening her knife on a rock is said to have made it bleed, revealing a Shiva lingam, and the temple was raised on that spot.

name: Thanthondreeswarar Temple, Woraiyur
significance: A Shiva temple attributed to the Pandya ruler Varaguna Pandiyan II in the 9th century, with inscriptions of 885 CE from the Chola period and a further record of a donation by a feudatory's queen in 911 CE under Parantaka I. It has a single prakaram and a two-tiered vimana but no gopuram, six daily services, and a bangle festival in the month of Thai as its chief celebration.
story: Shiva is said to have appeared here of his own accord as a lingam to grant the Chola queen Kanthimathi a safe delivery.

name: Chowalloor Siva Temple
significance: One of the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala and one of five Shiva shrines ringing Guruvayur. Its sanctum carries a copper roof with a golden finial, and a Subrahmanya shrine was added in renovations in 2001.
story: Folklore holds that the sage Parashurama installed the Shiva image here.

name: Aneswaram Siva Temple
significance: A west-facing Shiva temple at Chemmappilly, about three kilometres from the Thriprayar temple, once owned by a Namboothiri illam and now under the Cochin Devaswom Board. The annual Vavu bali offering to ancestors is performed here.
story: The Thriprayar Thevar is said never to have passed Aneswaram silently on his village circuit, because this deity had once lent him paddy and coconut.

name: Umiya Mata Temple, Unjha
significance: The principal temple of Umiya, clan deity of the Kadava Patidars, at Unjha in Mehsana district; it marked its silver jubilee in November 2009 with Chief Minister Narendra Modi in attendance. The shrine is a fixture for politicians seeking Kadava Patidar support, and the community has founded related Umiya Mata temples abroad, including one at Macon, Georgia in 2013.
